title: Love Your Neighbor
lead: "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Leviticus 19:18) is a short line in a list of laws that became, for Jews and Christians, a summary of the whole law. Leviticus 19:34 applies the same words to the foreigner.

sections.h: From Leviticus to the New Testament
sections.b: Leviticus commands love for the neighbor (19:18) and for the foreigner (19:34). Rabbi Akiva called 19:18 a great principle of the Torah, and Hillel summed up the Torah as "what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow" (Talmud, Shabbat 31a). Jesus joins it to the Shema as the two great commandments (Mark 12:28–34; Matthew 22:34–40), answers "Who is my neighbor?" with the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25–37), and extends it to enemies (Matthew 5:43–48). Paul calls it the fulfillment of the law (Romans 13:8–10; Galatians 5:14), James "the royal law" (James 2:8), and John makes love of the brother the test of love for God (1 John 4:20–21).
